chapters.title: One issue. Two questions.
chapters.body:
Can we tell evidence from guesswork?
Import a GitHub issue. Ask what it says, then something it cannot know.
This makes an answer easier to check before you trust it.

chapters.title: Start with one real issue.
chapters.body:
We’re importing a proposal for a SQL template function.
The question will search this issue, not every document in the lab.

chapters.title: Find the reason in the source.
chapters.body:
The proposal describes a way to reuse SQL statements.
Ask how it works, then check the cited passage.

chapters.title: See where the knowledge lives.
chapters.body:
Open the source node. Its location and labeled connections
show how the document is represented in the graph.

chapters.step: 04 / ASK WHAT THE SOURCE CANNOT KNOW
chapters.title: Now test the boundary.
chapters.body:
What’s the weather in Tokyo?
A SQL proposal has no evidence for that answer.

chapters.title: Ask the first question again.
chapters.body:
An exact question and matching settings can reuse the graph cache.
The evidence stays attached; retrieval and generation can be skipped.

chapters.step: THE RESULT / TRY THE SAME EXPERIMENT
chapters.title: A source. A citation. A boundary.
chapters.body:
One supported answer. One honest refusal. One reusable result.
Try your own GitHub issue in the live lab.
